correctness.rationale: For \(L_i=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&b\\s_i&a_i\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), all rates are positive and \(0<a_i,s_i<1\). Direct multiplication yields \(T_{123}-T_{132}=b\det\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&a_1&s_1\\1&a_2&s_2\\1&a_3&s_3\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). Both three-factor products have determinant \(-b^3s_1s_2s_3\) and strictly positive entries, so their Perron roots are strictly ordered by their traces. For each cyclic order, the threshold polynomial \(1-a_1a_2a_3-bC_{\pi}-b^3\prod_i s_i\) has exactly one positive zero, with distinct zeros iff the demographic points are noncollinear. The exact rational example gives traces \(73/96\) and \(35/32\), common determinant \(-1/9\), and unit-characteristic values \(37/288\) and \(-59/288\). The two-factor order invariance is a characteristic-polynomial identity. Attached independent SymPy algebra and Fraction arithmetic checkers were executed successfully; the latter checked 1,728 additional rational cases, not as a substitute for proof.

originality.rationale: The checked primary literature provides the Leslie/stage-model framework, general ordered-periodic matrix growth and reproduction-number theory, and sensitivity calculations, but does not supply the specific sharp three-phase orientation classification or the iff interval of fecundities with opposite growth verdicts. The exact statement was compared with a close two-patch symmetrizable seasonal-mixing model and with distinct nonlinear scalar seasonal maps; neither entails the presented orientation law for the displayed stage matrices. Results using different commutator or age-structured terminology remain a residual risk.

value.rationale: The exact answer is motivated by seasonal survival scheduling in a standard two-stage population model and a shared fecundity management parameter. It classifies all six season orders, identifies the sharp minimum of three seasons, and gives an if-and-only-if geometric condition for the existence of a nonempty fecundity interval where the same environments yield opposite invasion outcomes. This is an interpretable structural classification, not a cherry-picked numerical detail; the claim does not extrapolate to stochastic or nonlinear real populations.
